primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Somatostatin-receptor signaling during octreotide treatment of acromegaly
mechanism: Octreotide is a somatostatin analogue that suppresses growth hormone secretion. Somatostatin receptors are G protein-coupled receptors that signal through inhibitory G proteins; a major downstream effect is inhibition of adenylyl cyclase with reduced intracellular cAMP. Somatostatin-receptor activation also reduces intracellular calcium and promotes other inhibitory signaling, collectively decreasing hormone secretion.
vignette: A 45-year-old man with acromegaly is treated with octreotide. After treatment, his growth hormone and insulin-like growth factor 1 concentrations decrease. The drug binds somatostatin receptors on pituitary somatotroph cells.
lead: Which of the following intracellular signaling changes is most directly expected after activation of these receptors?
correct: Activation of Gi with inhibition of adenylyl cyclase and decreased intracellular cAMP
distractors: Activation of Gs with stimulation of adenylyl cyclase and increased intracellular cAMP
Activation of Gq with phospholipase C stimulation and generation of IP3 and diacylglycerol
Activation of an intrinsic receptor tyrosine kinase with downstream PI3K-Akt signaling
Activation of a receptor-associated JAK kinase with downstream STAT signaling
distractor_notes: Gs-coupled receptors stimulate adenylyl cyclase and increase cAMP. Somatostatin receptors instead exert inhibitory signaling that includes Gi-mediated suppression of adenylyl cyclase.

Gq-coupled receptors activate phospholipase C, generating IP3 and diacylglycerol and increasing intracellular calcium. This is not the characteristic inhibitory G-protein pathway of somatostatin receptors.

Intrinsic receptor tyrosine kinases autophosphorylate after ligand binding and can activate pathways such as PI3K-Akt; the insulin receptor is a classic endocrine example. Somatostatin receptors are GPCRs rather than intrinsic receptor tyrosine kinases.
Some cytokine-family hormone receptors signal through receptor-associated JAK kinases and STAT proteins. Somatostatin receptors instead are inhibitory GPCRs.
key_expl: Octreotide exerts actions similar to somatostatin and suppresses growth hormone secretion. Somatostatin receptors are GPCRs coupled to inhibitory G proteins. Activation of Gi inhibits adenylyl cyclase, lowering intracellular cAMP; somatostatin-receptor activation also lowers intracellular calcium, reinforcing inhibition of secretory activity. The other options represent distinct receptor-signaling families rather than the somatostatin-receptor pathway.
objective: Connect somatostatin-receptor activation to Gi-mediated inhibition of adenylyl cyclase and reduced cAMP, explaining the inhibitory endocrine effect of octreotide in acromegaly.
